- audio_msgs/audio_samples received from the client

- send_audio_ok/send_audio_err from forwarding into the engine session
- text_msgs/close_msgs
- last_audio_ms

changes.from: Server-side inverse text normalization (ITN) pass for final transcripts
changes.to: Regex-capable replacement rules for text normalization (data-authored)

changes.from:
## Problem

No engine in eaRS performs deterministic inverse text normalization. Written-form numbers depend entirely on the model's learned habits:

- Kyutai: mostly spoken form ("ninety nine dollars")
- parakeet-rs multilingual Nemotron 3.5 (ArchVM dictation server): spoken form for most numbers/currency — confirmed in live dictation 2026-07-20
- parakeet-rs English nemotron-speech-en: mostly written form, but probabilistic/contextual
- transcribe.cpp Nemotron 3.5 port (planned engine): spoken form (benchmarked: "Ninety Nine point nine nine dollars" vs golden "$99.99"; ~9pp of long-clip WER on number-heavy audio)

## Proposal

Deterministic ITN pass server-side on **final** text segments (not partials), engine-independent, sitting next to the dictionary replacement stage so it fixes all current and future engines at once.

Scope: English + German from the start (dictation languages in use).
- numbers, ordinals, decimals ("point"/"Komma")
- currency ($, EUR: "ninety nine dollars ninety nine" / "neunundneunzig Euro neunundneunzig")
- years vs quantities heuristics ("nineteen ninety nine" -> 1999 in year context)
- percent, times, dates (stretch)

Implementation options to evaluate:
1. Rule/regex-based Rust module (simple, deterministic, testable) — likely sufficient
2. WFST approach a la nemo_text_processing (heavy, probably overkill)

Config: on by default for dictation, toggleable per session (like codec/language).

## Notes

- Must be idempotent and never touch already-written-form text.
- Golden-corpus WER harness in test_audio/ can gate regressions.
- Benchmark context: transcribe.cpp has ITN API surface (transcribe_itn_mode) but only SenseVoice/FunASR support it; Nemotron ITN there is not on any roadmap. Doing it in eaRS is engine-neutral.
changes.to:
Rescoped from "server-side EN+DE ITN rule engine" after a bitter-lesson audit: a compiled-in per-language ITN rule engine hand-codes linguistic knowledge that ASR checkpoints learn better each year (English Nemotron already emits written-form numbers natively), and supporting a new language would require recompiling eaRS.

New scope:
1. Extend the existing replacement/dictionary pipeline to support regex rules (pattern -> replacement with capture groups), authored as data in dictionary TOML files. eaRS stays a deterministic transform of (audio, rules) -> text; zero linguistic judgment compiled into the core.
2. Ship an optional example dictionary with common EN/DE spoken-number/currency normalizations so operators can opt in.
3. Document the model-selection fix: spoken-form output is primarily a checkpoint weakness (multilingual Nemotron 3.5); prefer written-form-strong models (English Nemotron, transcribe.cpp multitalker-parakeet) where possible.

Out of scope: any built-in per-language ITN engine. Long-tail multilingual ITN belongs in the judgment layer (Foxline LLM post-pass), not eaRS.

This no longer blocks transcribe.cpp integration (trx-ffpf) - that integration IS the scaling fix for written-form output.

changes.from:
## Decision (2026-07-20)

Adopt transcribe.cpp (handy-computer/transcribe.cpp, GGUF/ggml, Rust bindings in bindings/rust/) as an eaRS engine. Keep kyutai and parakeet-rs for now (sherpa removed in e27de31f). Long-term this may replace parakeet-rs entirely and add the offline (batch) transcription capability eaRS lacks; trnscrb could then use eaRS as a backend incl. context-aware dictionary.

## Benchmark evidence (M4 Max, golden corpus, Q8 Metal streaming 560ms)

| model | short WER | long WER | speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| eaRS parakeet-rs fp32 CPU (baseline) | 4.49% | 6.88% | 11x |
| tc nemotron-3.5 multilingual | 5.62% | 15.87% (no ITN) | 30x |
| tc multitalker-parakeet (EN) | 3.37% | 5.82% | 34x |
| tc nemotron-speech-en | 4.49% | 8.99% (no ITN) | 35x |
| tc voxtral-mini-realtime 4B | 1.12% | 5.29% | ~4.7x |
| tc moonshine-streaming tiny/medium | unusable | unusable | 1-3x |

Recommended defaults: multitalker-parakeet Q8 (EN, 734MB), nemotron-3.5 Q8 (multilingual). Voxtral optional quality-first single-session.

## Scope

- New engine module behind `transcribe-cpp` feature using the Rust bindings (vendored/pinned rev; upstream is v0.1.x, fast-moving)
- Streaming sessions via transcribe_stream_{begin,feed,finalize}; 24kHz->16kHz resample as in parakeet_rs.rs
- Offline/batch path for `ears -f` (new capability: run offline models incl. Whisper/Canary/Qwen3-ASR)
- Reuse server-side energy gate + pre-roll from parakeet_rs.rs (move above engine seam if practical)
- Per-language model selection like sherpa's old LANG=PATH scheme; session set_language switches model
- Concurrency caveat: one loaded model = one active inference (mutex); evaluate per-session instances vs queueing vs max_sessions
- justfile/config/schema/README updates

## Caveats

- No ITN for Nemotron family in tc — depends on trx-5xj3 (engine-neutral server-side ITN)
- Multitalker port is single_speaker_mode only today; speaker-attributed streaming (S1/S2 channels -> trnscrb embedding identity-mapping) is an upstream-tracking item
- CMake/C++ dep in build; replaces ORT dylib pain, does not add to it
changes.to:
Unblocked from trx-5xj3: ITN was rescoped to data-authored regex replacement rules and no longer gates engine work. Integrating transcribe.cpp (multitalker-parakeet Q8 for EN, nemotron-3.5 Q8 multilingual) is itself the primary fix for spoken-form output, since its best EN models emit written form natively.

Benchmarks (M4 Max, Q8, Metal, 560ms streaming): multitalker-parakeet 3.37%/5.82% WER ~34x RT; nemotron-3.5 5.62%/15.87% ~30x; voxtral-mini-realtime 1.12%/5.29% ~4.7x. Baseline eaRS parakeet-rs: 4.49%/6.88% ~11x.
